title: MimoSketch: A Framework to Mine Item Frequency on Multiple Nodes with Sketches

problem.claim: The work addresses item frequency mining in a distributed data-stream setting where multiple items are mined by multiple nodes.

contributions.claim: MimoSketch is a framework for item frequency estimation in the multiple-item, multiple-node scenario.
The framework combines an algorithm using random counting with mathematically proven unbiasedness and dynamically adaptive memory layout, together with a policy that schedules items across nodes.
The scheduling policy balances items among nodes to avoid overload and underload and improve overall mining accuracy.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that a prototype and evaluation improve item frequency estimation accuracy by an order of magnitude over state-of-the-art solutions.
The authors report that the scheduling policy further improves performance in multiple-node scenarios.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper frames distributed stream mining as a multiple-item, multiple-node problem.
It introduces MimoSketch to improve item frequency estimation.
The framework consists of an estimation algorithm and an item-scheduling policy.
The algorithm uses unbiased random counting and adaptive memory allocation, while scheduling balances item load across nodes.
The authors report order-of-magnitude accuracy improvement over state-of-the-art solutions and additional gains from scheduling.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the evaluation datasets, baselines, workload conditions, or metrics.
The abstract does not provide implementation, parameter, or reproducibility details.
The abstract does not quantify the scheduling policy's additional performance improvement.
